y-m-12-13.title: The highest month and the month with the biggest increase
y-m-12-13.topic: Telling apart the highest value and the interval with the biggest increase in a line graph
y-m-12-13.goal: Tell apart 'the value is the biggest' and 'it changed the most', design a table that makes changes easy to compare, and make your own data in which the two cases are different.
y-m-12-13.material: Daeun drew a line graph of the number of visitors per month (unit: people) at her town library. January 40, February 90, March 130, April 150, May 160. Points are marked for each month and neighboring points are joined by line segments. Daeun answered the question 'Which month had the biggest increase?' as below. There is a mistake in this solution.
y-m-12-13.thinking.0: Finding the wrong line in a solution
y-m-12-13.thinking.1: Designing a way to compare amounts of change
y-m-12-13.thinking.2: Making your own data that fits the conditions
y-m-12-13.prereq.0: How to read a line graph
y-m-12-13.prereq.1: Comparing the difference of two numbers
y-m-12-13.s.s1.prompt: Choose one wrong line in Daeun's solution.
y-m-12-13.s.s1.hint.0: Write down, one at a time, the difference showing how many people it grew by between each two neighboring months.
y-m-12-13.s.s1.hint.1: Compare whether finding the highest point and finding the steepest rising segment are the same thing.
y-m-12-13.s.s1.line.0: The value for May, 160, is the highest.
y-m-12-13.s.s1.line.1: So the visitors increased the most in May.
y-m-12-13.s.s1.line.2: Going from April to May the segment rises to the upper right, so it is true that it increased.
y-m-12-13.s.s1.line.3: From January to February it went from 40 to 90, so it did not increase much.
y-m-12-13.s.s1.explain: Line 2 is wrong. The month with the highest value and the month with the biggest increase may not be the same. Line 4 is also wrong. From January to February it grew by 50 people, the biggest increase among neighboring months (February→March 40 people, March→April 20 people, April→May 10 people).
y-m-12-13.s.s2.prompt: Daeun wants to add one more row to the table so she can compare 'how much it grew each month' at a glance. Which row is most suitable?
y-m-12-13.s.s2.hint.0: First decide whether what you want to know is 'size' or 'change'.
y-m-12-13.s.s2.hint.1: Check whether each row tells the difference between months.
y-m-12-13.s.s2.o.a: The increase compared with the previous month
y-m-12-13.s.s2.r.a: If you write the difference from the previous month for each month, you can compare the change right away.
y-m-12-13.s.s2.o.b: The sum of the number of visitors for all months
y-m-12-13.s.s2.r.b: A total tells the whole but does not show the change between months.
y-m-12-13.s.s2.o.c: A mark for the month with the most visitors
y-m-12-13.s.s2.r.c: The month with the most can already be seen from the graph, and it does not help with comparing change.
y-m-12-13.s.s2.o.d: The order from most to fewest visitors
y-m-12-13.s.s2.r.d: The order is used for comparing size and does not show change.
y-m-12-13.s.s2.explain: If you put 'the increase compared with the previous month' as a row, you can compare the change between months right away. Rows that show the size of the values are less useful for comparing change.
y-m-12-13.s.s3.prompt: This time, make data from January to April in which the number of visitors is highest in the third month (March), and the interval with the biggest increase is from January to February. The number of visitors is a natural number from 0 to 200. Call the monthly values p1, p2, p3, p4. Make 2 different sets of data.
y-m-12-13.s.s3.hint.0: First set March as the highest. Then set February and April lower than March.
y-m-12-13.s.s3.hint.1: Make January low so that the increase from January to February is bigger than that from February to March and from March to April.
y-m-12-13.s.s3.ok.c1: All values are natural numbers from 0 to 200.
y-m-12-13.s.s3.fail.c1: Write the number of visitors as a natural number from 0 to 200.
y-m-12-13.s.s3.ok.c3: The biggest increase was between January and February.
y-m-12-13.s.s3.fail.c3: The biggest increase was not between January and February.
y-m-12-13.s.s3.explain: For example, with 10, 60, 80, 70, the highest month is March (80), but the interval with the biggest increase is January to February (50 people). The data showed that the highest value and the interval with the biggest increase can be different.

y-m-12-14.title: When did the temperatures of the two villages become equal?
y-m-12-14.topic: The crossing of two line graphs (the meaning of the hidden times in between)
y-m-12-14.goal: Tell apart the values at the measured times and the values guessed by joining the points in between, and revise your guess when a new measurement arrives.
y-m-12-14.material: On the same day, the temperatures of Village 가 and Village 나 were measured only twice, at 10 a.m. and 12 noon (unit: °C). Village 가 is 20°C at 10 and 24°C at 12. Village 나 is 24°C at 10 and 22°C at 12. When the points of each village were joined by line segments on the same graph, the two segments cross each other between 10 and 12. Assume that the temperature does not jump suddenly between 10 and 12 either, but keeps changing continuously.
y-m-12-14.thinking.0: Telling apart what is certain from the data and what needs an assumption
y-m-12-14.thinking.1: Evaluating a claim that states a guess as if it were certain
y-m-12-14.thinking.2: Revising a guess with new data
y-m-12-14.prereq.0: Reading values from a line graph
y-m-12-14.s.s1.hint.0: First compare which village was higher at 10 and at 12.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.hint.1: Sort each statement into: read directly from the measured values, needs an assumption, or has no ground.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.o.a: At 10, Village 나 was 4°C higher than Village 가
y-m-12-14.s.s1.r.a: It is the difference between the measured values 24 and 20. You can read it from the directly measured values.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.r.b: It was not measured at 11. Even if you guess by joining with segments, they are not equal at 11.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.o.c: At 12, Village 가 was 2°C higher than Village 나
y-m-12-14.s.s1.r.c: It is the difference between the measured values 24 and 22. You can read it from the directly measured values.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.r.d: You said it using both the fact that the order switched and the assumption that 'it changes continuously'.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.o.e: Between 10 and 12, the temperature difference between the two villages stayed 4°C
y-m-12-14.s.s1.r.e: At 10 the difference was 4°C, but at 12 Village 가 became higher, so the difference changed.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.explain: a and c are measured values. d says that Village 나 is higher at 10 and Village 가 is higher at 12, so if the temperature changed continuously, there was a time in between when they became equal. b is a value at 11 that was not measured, so it has no ground, and e does not match the value at 12.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.prompt: Yuri said, 'If you calculate where the two segments meet, it is around 11:20, and the temperature then is about 22.7°C.' How should we see this statement?
y-m-12-14.s.s2.hint.0: Check whether there is a directly measured value at 11:20.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.hint.1: Think about whether the temperature could go up and down between the two points.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.o.a: You can say it is a settled fact, the same as a value measured at 11:20
y-m-12-14.s.s2.r.a: It was not measured at 11:20. It is a value calculated by joining two points.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.o.d: The calculation is right, so if we measure at 11:20 it will definitely be 22.7°C
y-m-12-14.s.s2.r.d: There is no guarantee that the change in between is steady. If actually measured, it could be different.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.explain: A value calculated by joining two points with a straight line is a guess that 'it could be so'. It matches reality only if the assumption that the temperature changed at a steady rate is right.
y-m-12-14.s.s3.prompt: I measured once more at 11, and Village 가 was 21°C and Village 나 was 23.5°C. After learning this new value, how should you revise your thinking about when the temperatures of the two villages became equal? Write using the new value as evidence.
y-m-12-14.s.s3.hint.0: First compare which village was higher at 11.
y-m-12-14.s.s3.hint.1: Combine it with which village was higher at 12, and think about around when they became equal.
y-m-12-14.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did you use the new values (21°C, 23.5°C) as evidence?
y-m-12-14.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did you compare which village was higher at 11?
y-m-12-14.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Did you also think that you would need to measure more to know the exact time?
y-m-12-14.s.s3.model.0: At 11, Village 가 is 21°C and Village 나 is 23.5°C, so Village 나 was still higher. At 12, Village 가 is higher, so the time they became equal changes to between 11 and 12. 11:20 was wrong.
y-m-12-14.s.s3.model.1: The first guess (around 11:20) must be revised. Village 나 was still 2.5°C higher at 11 too, so the time they became equal is after 11. To know the exact time, you need to measure more often.
y-m-12-14.s.s3.modelNote.1: It also said that more measuring is needed.
